question.text: The height of liquid column raised in a capillary tube of certain radius when dipped in liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> vertically is, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If the tube is dipped in a similar manner in another liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of surface tension and density double the values of liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>, the height of liquid column raised in liquid B would be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The height h through which a liquid will rise in a capillary tube of radius r is given by,

h=2Tcosθrρg∝Tρ∝2T2ρ

As we can see in both cases, value of height will remain same. Therefore,

h'=h=5 cm= 0.05 m
